documents.purpose: Mean Mars surface phase function from Mars Express OMEGA and MRO CRISM with the atmosphere removed, used to light the Viking MDIM 2.1 map, which is itself surface only.

references.evidence: Vincendon (2013) parameterizes the mean surface phase function with Hapke (1993): w 0.85, theta 17 degrees, c 0.6, b 0.12, B0 1, h 0.05, with c = (1 + c_Hapke)/2 as Johnson et al. (2006a), the ISIS two-term Henyey-Greenstein weighting. The paper states that phase angles below 70 degrees and emergence 0-70 degrees constrain the surface, and that the shape holds across solar wavelengths.
references.locator: Abstract; section 2.1

documents.purpose: Limb halo profile: PSG radiance on limb lines of sight by tangent altitude with the Sun behind the observer, and the nadir radiance under an overhead Sun, in the red (640-670 nm), green (530-560 nm) and blue (440-490 nm) bands. The halo starts at the surface.

references.evidence: PSG computes limb and tangential lines of sight with single scattering only (https://psg.gsfc.nasa.gov/images/help/handbook.pdf, p. 96), so these limb calls use NMAX 0 and LMAX 43, the phase-function length PSG asks for the Mars aerosols. PUMAS falls back to a plane-parallel two-stream solver that ignores the tangent altitude when (LMAX+1) x layers x (aerosols+3) x spectral points passes 1e9, so each band is the mean of 10 nm windows, and every answer's method line was checked. With the Sun on the tangent point horizon the single-scattering path is dark, so the Sun sits one degree above it (solar zenith 89 degrees), behind the observer.
references.locator: Handbook chapter 5, section 5 'Specifics of multiple scattering simulations', 'Limb and tangential simulations', p. 96
